message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
W2's report: {"refunds_applied": [{"order_id": 214, "amount_cents": 6668}, {"order_id": 213, "amount_cents": 15133}], "failed": [{"order_id": 211, "amount_cents": 12701, "error": "write failed: disk I/O error, refund not recorded (failed on 3 attempts; list_refunds confirms it is not recorded)"}]}
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to confirm the refunds table matches the refunds Alpha reported. I'll start by listing the refunds.

The refunds table matches Alpha's applied list exactly (orders 213 and 214, same amounts), and failed order 211 is absent, so there is no mismatch to hold on. Next I need the customer list, so I'll fetch the orders.

The refunds table matches Alpha's applied list (orders 213 and 214 at the same amounts), and failed order 211 is absent, so there is no mismatch to hold on. Next I'll get the net balance for the first customer, acme.
acme's net balance of 48125 is consistent with its orders (31647 + 31611) minus refund 213 (15133). Next I'll get birch's net balance.

birch's net of 67298 matches its orders (38685 + 35281) minus refund 214 (6668), and the failed refund for order 211 is correctly excluded since it was never recorded. Last customer is cobalt, so I'll fetch its net balance.

All three net balances are in and consistent with the orders and the verified refunds table (cobalt's 46961 equals 32516 + 14445 with no refunds). The refunds match Alpha's report, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme at 48125.
Acme's payout of 48125 is recorded. Next I'll record birch's payout at its verified net balance of 67298.
Acme and birch are paid. Cobalt's verified net balance is 46961, which matches its orders (32516 + 14445) with no refunds, so I'll record that payout now.
All three payouts have been recorded and each returned ok. The refunds matched Alpha's report, so the batch is complete and I'll finish with the payout map.
